new.title: A fixed 32 by 32 bipartite graph given by its table: some AND/OR/NOT circuit of fan-in at most two with at most 128 gates is right whenever one row and one column are on
new.statement: ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ C.size ≤ 128 ∧ PEqualNP.Represents.Represents (fun u v : Fin 32 => (([0xf2bc7573, 0x59092a9d, 0xc443c8c2, 0x1d58483a, 0x1b7982bb, 0xa8882290, 0x74d0fd25, 0x00041402, 0x6879a8a5, 0xd65a6f1a, 0x7455fba3, 0x24508c1a, 0x3050a010, 0x68658ad5, 0x10a00735, 0x5e55690e, 0x6ab804a4, 0x00b01458, 0xf447af40, 0x00b07351, 0xa88c2290, 0x40d9d7bc, 0x40241486, 0x54058082, 0x6891afb9, 0x50ddf79e, 0x553080be, 0x28c180f8, 0x6ac8ae9e, 0xa6860e80, 0x20508c18, 0x10f01050] : List ℕ).getD u.val 0).testBit v.val) C
new.unlocks: a circuit under the count we hold for this graph; how low the count goes is what we want to learn
new.context: We hold 255 gates for this table: one AND of two ORs for each key, all ORed. Only the gate list is checked. No sorry, no new axiom. Own namespace for every declaration.
new.sketch: Row u of the table, as a hex number, is entry u of the list in the statement; bit v is set when row u is joined to column v. The table comes from a keyed mixing rule of ours (k = 5). We hold 255 gates: for each key, the OR of its rows AND the OR of its columns, all ORed; sharing those ORs between keys brings ours to 225 (computed). Answer with a gate list; it is checked by one evaluation per promise input (1024). Any method. A prover can use represents_of_pcols in lean/PEqualNP/Library/Helpers/PromiseCol.lean. At 128, four gates a side-vertex: truth unknown to us.

changed.context: No witness is known to us; this is a search; two NOT gates or an input read twice are possible here. The other twenty masks of the first break step are covered by a separate 'none exists' form. No sorry, no new axiom. Own namespace for every declaration.

changed.title: Small cases only: for every n at least 3, an n by n bipartite graph is represented with at most 2n - 4 more AND/OR gates of fan-in two than its complement
changed.statement: ∀ (n s : ℕ) (A : Fin n → Fin n → Bool), 3 ≤ n → PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost (fun u v => !A u v) s → PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost A (s + (2 * n - 4))
changed.unlocks: whether a NOT gate at the output can save more than 2n - 4 gates, for the NOT-gate transfer line
changed.context: Small cases only. Truth open; its literal negation is posted beside it. It is the NOT-at-the-output half of 'c at most t + 2n - 5': a circuit whose one NOT is its output costs the complement's AND/OR cost plus 1. On the line at every n on two checked families: the graph missing one cell, and the block against the cross. Tables, computed, not checked: largest gap 2 at side 3 and 4 at side 4. One graph whose complement is cheaper by 2n - 3 breaks it. A break-it of its own cannot exist: its literal negation is posted beside it.

changed.context: Small cases only. Truth open; the statement it negates is posted beside it. changed.title: For every n at least 3, an n by n graph with an AND/OR circuit of s gates has a complement with one of at most s + 2n - 4 gates, fan-in two
changed.statement: ∀ (n s : ℕ) (G : Fin n → Fin n → Bool), 3 ≤ n → (∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 C ∧ PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (n + n) C ∧ C.size ≤ s ∧ PEqualNP.Represents.Represents G C) → ∃ D : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 D ∧ PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (n + n) D ∧ D.size ≤ s + 2 * n - 4 ∧ PEqualNP.Represents.Represents (fun u v => !(G u v)) D
changed.unlocks: a statement about NOT gates with no NOT gate in it: it bounds what one NOT gate at the top of a circuit can save
changed.context: A conjecture; we hold no argument. The unit beside it on unions of complete pieces gives it for those graphs; a proof must handle a connected graph with a connected complement, where no classes exist. Computed, not checked: at side 4 every class with both costs computed differs by at most 4 (305 pairs, two seats' code); at side 5 the matching against the crown sits exactly on it. It fails at n = 2, hence n from 3. The opposite unit stands beside it. A companion cannot exist as a unit: the statement is about every graph of its kind. Size: hours, if an argument exists.

changed.context: The opposite of a conjecture of ours; we hold no witness; this is a search for one graph. changed.statement: PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost (fun (u : Fin 5) (v : Fin 5) => (32435687 : ℕ).testBit (5 * u.val + v.val)) 14
changed.unlocks: whether one named graph sits on or under the open pair's line on the AND/OR side
changed.context: A search. We hold an AND/OR circuit of 15 gates (the crown less a cell in at most 4n - 5, at n = 5; computed). The crown itself costs exactly 15 (a checked row), and the removed cell drops one AND term that the crown's chain shares, so its prefix ORs may serve the cut row with one gate fewer; at side 4 the least value was one below the hand move. What a circuit of 14 decides: by checked rows alone, nothing (a saving of at most 14 - 8 = 6); with the n + m - 2 transfer, a conjecture, it puts the graph on or under the line. We hold no circuit of 14 gates; this is a search.

changed.sketch: We hold no circuit of 150 gates; this is a search. A circuit smaller than our checked one would share subcircuits across rows: the rule's rounds act the same way on every row up to the key, so the ORs of the row sets of keys (one per key) can be built once and reused, and rows whose key sets overlap share their unions. Answer with a gate list (AND, OR or NOT, each reading at most two wires) and its output wire; only the gate list is checked, on the 1024 inputs with one row and one column on.
